questions.text:
Choose the most appropriate logical connector to join the sentences.
Sentence 1: He was severely injured in the accident.
Sentence 2: He managed to drag himself to safety.
questions.explanation: The two sentences show a contrast. Being severely injured usually prevents someone from moving, but he managed to move anyway. "Nevertheless" perfectly indicates this unexpected contrast.

questions.text:
Choose the most appropriate logical connector to join the sentences.
Sentence 1: The company has seen a significant decline in revenue this quarter.
Sentence 2: They are planning to lay off twenty percent of their workforce.
questions.explanation: The second sentence is a direct result or consequence of the first sentence (decline in revenue leads to layoffs). "Consequently" is the correct connector.

questions.text:
Choose the most appropriate logical connector to join the sentences.
Sentence 1: You must submit the application by Friday.
Sentence 2: Your candidacy will not be considered for the position.
questions.explanation: The second sentence presents a negative alternative or consequence if the condition in the first sentence is not met. "Otherwise" expresses this condition correctly.

questions.text:
Choose the most appropriate logical connector to join the sentences.
Sentence 1: The novel is highly praised for its intricate plot.
Sentence 2: It is admired for its deep character development.
questions.explanation: The second sentence adds another positive point to the first positive point. "Furthermore" is used to add more information of a similar nature.

questions.text:
Choose the most appropriate logical connector to join the sentences.
Sentence 1: The traffic was heavily congested on the main highway.
Sentence 2: We took a scenic detour through the countryside.
questions.explanation: Taking a detour was the result of the heavy traffic. "Hence" means "as a consequence" or "for this reason".

questions.text:
Choose the most appropriate logical connector to join the sentences.
Sentence 1: She prepared diligently for the entrance examination for months.
Sentence 2: She failed to achieve the minimum qualifying score.
questions.explanation: There is a strong contrast between preparing diligently and failing. "Yet" acts as a coordinating conjunction indicating contrast (meaning "but nevertheless").

questions.text:
Choose the most appropriate logical connector to join the sentences.
Sentence 1: The diet requires you to cut out all processed sugars.
Sentence 2: You must drink at least three liters of water daily.
questions.explanation: The second sentence adds another rule or requirement to the diet. "Additionally" serves to add this supplementary information.

questions.text:
Choose the most appropriate logical connector to join the sentences.
Sentence 1: The climate in this region is incredibly harsh and arid.
Sentence 2: Certain species of cacti thrive here all year round.
questions.explanation: The harsh climate makes survival difficult, but cacti survive anyway. "Even so" means "in spite of that" and introduces a surprising contrast.

questions.text:
Choose the most appropriate logical connector to join the sentences.
Sentence 1: Artificial intelligence has automated many rudimentary tasks.
Sentence 2: It has inadvertently created a demand for highly skilled data scientists.
questions.explanation: The two effects of artificial intelligence (automating tasks and creating demand) are happening at the same time. "Simultaneously" correctly connects these parallel events.

questions.text:
Choose the most appropriate logical connector to join the sentences.
Sentence 1: He lacked the formal educational qualifications required for the job.
Sentence 2: His vast practical experience made him the ideal candidate.
questions.explanation: The two sentences present two contrasting perspectives on his suitability for the job. "On the other hand" is used to introduce a contrasting point of view.

questions.text:
Choose the most appropriate logical connector to join the sentences.
Sentence 1: The central bank drastically lowered the interest rates.
Sentence 2: The inflation rate soared to an unprecedented high.
questions.explanation: "As a corollary" means as a direct or natural consequence or result. If inflation soared as a result of lowering interest rates, this connector fits perfectly. (Wait, let's look at the options. Is it a consequence? Lowering interest rates causes inflation. Yes, it's a consequence).

questions.text:
Choose the most appropriate logical connector to join the sentences.
Sentence 1: The proposal was extremely lucrative and beneficial for the firm.
Sentence 2: The board of directors vetoed it over ethical concerns.
questions.explanation: The proposal was good, but it was vetoed. "Notwithstanding" means "in spite of this" or "nevertheless", which correctly bridges the contrast. (Note: "Albeit" means although, but it connects clauses internally, not two independent sentences easily without restructuring).

questions.text:
Choose the most appropriate logical connector to join the sentences.
Sentence 1: The initial trials of the vaccine showed an 80% efficacy rate.
Sentence 2: Further testing revealed dangerous long-term side effects.
questions.explanation: The first sentence is highly positive (high efficacy). The second sentence is highly negative (dangerous side effects). "Conversely" introduces a statement or idea which reverses one that has just been made.

questions.text:
Choose the most appropriate logical connector to join the sentences.
Sentence 1: Stringent cybersecurity protocols were implemented across the network.
Sentence 2: A massive data breach compromised millions of user accounts.
questions.explanation: Strict protocols were put in place, but a breach happened anyway. "Nonetheless" means "in spite of that", serving as the perfect contrast connector.
